newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks choppy at open, Michelin drops.
newsitem.headline: French stocks choppy at open, Michelin drops.

text.p: French shares struggled to find support after easing at the opening on Tuesday, following Monday's savage pruning which clipped two percent off the CAC stock index.
Traders said the market was cautious after the Dow's sharp swings, which closed up 20 points after dropping 80 in the day.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 3.15 points or 0.12 percent at 2,585.23 at 0915 GMT, while the CAC-40 futures contract was down 10 at 2,585 from Monday's close.

Michelin dropped in heavy volume, down 3.42 percent after 30 minutes of trading, and was among the biggest turnover stocks. A broker said the tyre-maker disappointed with a net attributable profit of 2.89 billion francs, which included a 845 million restructuring charge.
A market consensus had been looking for a median of 3.4 billion.
Alcatel Alsthom pleased the market with its results, said to be "in line with estimates" with net income at 2.7 billion francs. The engineering group forecast satisfactory profit for 1998.

Cie de Suez fell 2.75 percent to 272 francs, Lyonnaise des Eaux was also weak, down 1.22 percent to 568. Analysts are preparing reports to clients on a rumoured merger between the two groups, with some speculating on a share exchange of two Suez shares for every one Lyonnaise share.
Thomson-CSF among rare risers, up 1.23 percent at 189 francs, with positive sentiment on pending privatisation.
Legrand also bucks trend, up 1.2 percent. A senior equity salesman said the stock was undervalued relative to the market.
